_note: Append-only. One entry per accepted release or reviewed amendment; one change item per agent-relevant semantic change. Entries carry NO commit identifier — a consumer derives the introducing commit from Git history at the target OID. Historical entries are never rewritten; a correction ships as a new amendment entry. Authoring rules: docs/release-ledger-authoring-guide.md.

entries.agent_impact: The QA Verdict and its committed sidecar projection now have hashed schema files a consumer can validate against, and the trust semantics of readback records are documented: trusted/trust_level/verified_at are receiver-stamped, trusted: false marks an anonymous submission, and every readback consumer must filter or segregate untrusted records. run-record verdict inference and sidecar promotion now enforce that segregation. Nothing existing changed shape; adoption is optional and additive.

changes.summary: The full QA verdict schema was introduced (contract identity campaigns-os-qa-verdict/v0; emitted schema_version literal "1.0"), derived from the emitting code and validated against real emitted verdicts. It documents the receiver-stamped trust fields and requires consumers to tolerate unknown additive fields.

The committed qa-verdict.json sidecar projection schema was introduced: same "1.0" schema_version literal as the full verdict, with the projection guarantees pinned — generated_at, emptied URL-bearing fields, the per-assertion allowlist, and the impossibility of receiver trust stamps.

The QA Verdict and sidecar-projection version lines were declared, including the rule that the emitted schema_version literal stays "1.0" and cannot change without a breaking shape change.

A Verdict schema and trust semantics section was added: what trusted: false means (an anonymous, unattributed submission), that shape validity is not trust, and that every downstream readback consumer must filter on trusted or segregate untrusted records.

run-record automatic QA-verdict inference now excludes records stamped trusted: false, and qa promote refuses to project an untrusted source verdict into the committed sidecar; an operator-explicit --qa-verdict path is still honored as given. No command, subcommand, or flag was added, renamed, or removed.

entries.agent_impact: The certified-template gate, doctor, and standardization report now also state each certified family’s last-verified SDK version and its delta from the current SDK, read from new per-family verification blocks on the vendored commerce surface catalog snapshot. Purely additive output: no command, flag, artifact schema, or exit-code behavior changed, and nothing that passed before fails now. A consumer may optionally read the new assembly.template_certification.freshness warning code and the catalog families[].verification blocks.

entries.agent_impact: The doctor command now blocks unprepared source HTML: mapped source pages with unstripped document wrappers or leftover/broken YAML frontmatter fail doctor with source_html.prep.document_wrapper / source_html.prep.frontmatter_residue errors (status blocked, next.stage collect-inputs), and source-file internal links warn as source_html.prep.internal_link_unrooted. Agents feeding raw full-document HTML into start/build must prepare the source per docs/quickstart.md "Prepare Raw HTML Source" or record wrapper_policy "preserve_document_wrappers" as an explicit adapter decision. Doctor issue codes remain governed by the ops-repo ADR-003 parity baseline, not the supported-surface manifest, so surface_version does not move.

changes.summary: doctor (and the doctor embedded in start/build) gained the source_html.preparation check: deterministic classification of common unprepared-source failures with actionable source_html.prep.* codes, each carrying a docs pointer; no argv change.

entries.agent_impact: The prepare-build/start certified-template gate now prints the certification-freshness stderr line for any decided family present on the vendored catalog, including a family whose certification was waived via --allow-uncertified-template; the waived line is prefixed "certification waived — " so agents parsing gate output can distinguish it from the certified-gate line. The doctor source-preparation check gained a third source_html.prep.frontmatter_residue variant, unterminated_embedded_block (severity error), for an embedded frontmatter block that never closes before EOF — source that previously passed doctor with this residue now blocks. Freshness rendering is hardened (null-safe, malformed verified_at omitted) and standardization reports warn once per run when catalog resolution fails instead of hiding the missing freshness field silently. No argv or schema change.

changes.summary: prepare-build (and the start intake alias) emits the certification-freshness line for any catalog-present family — labeled "certification waived — " when certification was waived — instead of only for certified families; no argv change.

entries.agent_impact: A consumer may now read a declarative, schema-validated description of how a checkout at a resolved commit becomes a usable installed runtime, and enforce it: exact commands, accepted Node and npm ranges, per-step network policy, the enumerated input set, seven mandatory output checks, and five bounds. It is data only — this repository publishes the recipe and executes no step of it. Enforcement is fail-closed: an unrecognized recipe kind, revision, or safety-critical enum is refused, and a check that cannot be performed counts as failed rather than skipped. Two readings a consumer must not take: the input set is the compiler's resolved file list rather than its configured globs, and campaign-spec/dist is a build output with no committed baseline, so output verification is self-consistency rather than comparison against a hash published here. A prepared generation can build and type-check but cannot run browser QA. Nothing existing changed shape; adoption is optional and additive.

changes.summary: The entry point now points at the runtime recipe as a separate contract from orientation, with the rules that come with it: execute only the enumerated commands, refuse an unrecognized kind or safety-critical enum, and do not read "runtime ready" as "can run browser QA".

The runtime-recipe schema was introduced (contract identity campaigns-os-runtime-recipe/v1). It accepts unknown additive fields while keeping required fields, known types, and safety-critical enums strict: recipe kind, revision major, step id, package manager, lifecycle-script disposition, network policy, output-check kind, engines-disagreement disposition, and the unperformable-check disposition all fail closed.

The accepted recipe instance was introduced, kind campaigns-os-node-v1 revision 1.0.0: the exact argv of both steps, Node >=20.19.0 <25 and npm major 10 or 11 with refusal on disagreement with the target's engines, a registry allowlist on install and denial on build, 42 enumerated inputs, seven mandatory output checks, and five enforced bounds each carrying its measured baseline.
The runtime readiness guide was introduced, generated from the recipe rather than hand-written, so a stale copy fails CI instead of misleading a reader.

surface_version advanced to 1.16.0; the runtime-recipe schema and the recipe instance were added as hashed entries, and the readiness guide, seventeen runtime-recipe fixtures, and three hostile-target fixture paths as named entries.
The compatibility promise now covers the runtime recipe and its fixtures, and records why the recipe is hashed while the orientation policy contracts beside it are named.
The runtime-recipe schema, kind, and revision version lines were declared, along with the rule separating a new kind (which gates on a consumer release) from a revision (which does not).

The runtime-recipe contract gate, its test suite, and the generated-documentation staleness check were added to npm run check, with check:runtime-recipe, check:runtime-docs, and generate:runtime-docs as their own scripts. No export, bin, engine, or dependency changed.
Regenerated for the 1.16.0 surface: the supported-surface-at-generation-time line advanced. No contract content changed.

The runtime-recipe fixture manifest was introduced, enumerating every accept and reject fixture with the outcome it must produce, so a consumer's parser test asserts an exact expected set rather than a hand-copied list.

The prepared-runtime state fixture was introduced: the healthy control plus the absent, extra, corrupt, and stale states an output-check implementation must distinguish, described declaratively so a test derives them from the recipe rather than from written-down paths.
An accepted runtime-recipe fixture a consumer's parser validates against: accept/current.json. The accepted recipe as published. A consumer's parser must accept exactly these bytes.

An accepted runtime-recipe fixture a consumer's parser validates against: accept/minimal.json. Required fields only, every optional field and authoring note stripped. Proves the required set is genuinely sufficient rather than accidentally propped up by optional content.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-kind.json. recipe_kind names a kind this schema version does not define. An installed consumer was not released knowing how to execute it, so it fails closed rather than guessing that a v2 is a v1 with extras.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-revision.json. recipe_revision leaves the major line the kind defines. A revision may only re-parameterise fields the consumer already understands; a different major is a shape change wearing a revision's clothes.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-network-policy.json. A safety-critical enum: the install step declares a network policy outside the defined set. There is no allow-all value, and an unrecognized one is refused rather than treated as permissive.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/allowlist-without-hosts.json. An allowlist with no hosts is not a bound, it is an empty declaration that reads like one. The schema requires a non-empty host list whenever the policy is an allowlist.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-output-check.json. A safety-critical enum: an output check names a kind the consumer cannot perform. A new KIND of check is a new recipe kind, because an installed consumer cannot perform a check it was not released knowing.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-step-id.json. A safety-critical enum: a step identity outside the defined set. Steps are identified rather than positional, so an unrecognized id is a command the consumer has no contract for.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/lifecycle-scripts-enabled.json. A safety-critical enum: a step that permits lifecycle scripts. Enabling them would let the target run arbitrary code during preparation, which is the single thing the recipe's flags exist to prevent.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/engines-disagreement-warns.json. A safety-critical enum: disagreement between the contract's tool range and the target's declared engines resolved as a warning. An accept-with-warning path produces a build made under conditions nobody approved.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/advisory-enforcement.json. fail_closed switched off. Advisory bounds record the right numbers and enforce nothing, so the first time a bound matters you discover it was decorative.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unperformable-check-skipped.json. A safety-critical enum: a check that cannot be performed treated as skipped. A skipped check reports success it never established.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/committed-output-claim.json. The recipe claims its output directory is a committed artifact. It is not: the directory is git-ignored and untracked, so no baseline for its contents can exist here and verification must be self-consistency.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unpinned-lockfile.json. The recipe claims its lockfile is not integrity-pinned. The network allowlist bounds where bytes may come from and the lockfile's digests bound which bytes are acceptable; dropping the second leaves the first standing alone, which it was never meant to do.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/missing-required-field.json. The enumerated input set is absent. Without it there is nothing to fingerprint, and staleness — the one failure mode no output-side check can see — becomes undetectable.

A second invariant was added beside the orientation one: recipe_execution declares that preparing this target runs the recipe's two steps and no lifecycle script reachable from them, names the intended-script log and the control, and enumerates the new dependency-side tripwires. The orientation tripwire set and its expected hit count of zero are unchanged.

Pre and post siblings of the build script were added as tripwires, the build script itself as the one intended script, and a dependency on the packed tripwire package, so a preparation run exercises dependency and pre/post lifecycle scripts for real.
The tripwire now takes an optional label so a hit says which script fired; called with no argument it emits the original line verbatim, so an existing counter matching that text keeps working.

The one script a recipe build step is meant to run. Not a tripwire: it logs to its own file so "the intended script ran" and "nothing else ran" stay separable, and a fixture that only proved emptiness cannot pass by never building at all.

A miniature dependency declaring every lifecycle script npm can run on a dependency. It is packed into a tarball and installed from it, so it is extracted the way a registry package is rather than symlinked the way a directory dependency is.
The dependency-side tripwire, self-contained because once packed it is extracted into node_modules where nothing else in the fixture is reachable.

entries.agent_impact: A fourth checkpoint gate is registered, built_output.upsell_selector_scope, and it can block a doctor run that previously passed. It fires when a built page whose funnel role is upsell or downsell carries a data-next-bundle-selector that lacks data-next-upsell-context and is in the default swap selection mode: such a selector writes to the shopper's live cart at init, so loading the page charges them for a package at the next checkout without it appearing in that checkout's rendered order summary. Two consequences a consumer must plan for. First, `doctor --built` can now return blocked; it previously only produced warnings, and a consumer treating that mode as advisory will need to read its exit state. Second, all eight certified template families (apollo, apollo-mv-single-step, demeter, olympus, olympus-mv-single-step, olympus-mv-two-step, shop-single-step, shop-three-step) currently ship a display-only selector with neither attribute across 19 upsell offer includes, so a campaign built from any certified family blocks until the templates are repaired upstream in campaign-cart-starter-templates. The remedy is to add data-next-upsell-context to the named selector, or to record a bounded named-human waiver through `campaigns-os checkpoint waive --gate built_output.upsell_selector_scope`. data-next-selection-mode="select" also clears the blocker and reports a warning instead, because the SDK gates every cart write on swap mode.

changes.summary: `checkpoint waive --gate` accepts a fourth registered gate, built_output.upsell_selector_scope, and doctor evaluates it in the built-output phase on both the packet path and `doctor --built`. The gate is reported in derived.checkpoint_gates and in the `next` gate summary like the three before it, and `doctor --built` can now return a blocked status rather than only warnings.

A lifecycle step was added for resolving the upsell selector-scope checkpoint, stating what an unscoped selector does to a shopper, that the gate runs on every doctor invocation rather than only after assembly, and the exact waiver command. Subsequent steps renumbered; version 1.0.6.
next-campaigns-os advanced to 1.0.6 for the added checkpoint step.

The `checkpoint` command's registered-gate list now names four gates rather than three. The support boundary is unchanged: registered gates may still grow beneath the listed command without a surface_version advance.
The packet-local checkpoint preflight now lists four registered checkpoints, and the waiver example's --gate alternation includes built_output.upsell_selector_scope.

entries.agent_impact: Two `qa resolve` outputs that could be believed no longer can be. First, `status: ready` now asserts that the derived entry URLs were probed AND resolved; it previously asserted only that they were derived from the packet, so a route set that was 100% dead reported ready with a next command that could not succeed. A consumer reading resolve status must handle two new terminal values: `routes_unresolved` (probed, at least one route dead, `ok: false`, first failing URL named, `qa run` suggestion suppressed) and `ready_unprobed` (routes existed but none produced a response, `ok: true`). Both are additive; the existing three values keep their meaning over probed-and-resolved routes. The status ladder is ordered by verification coverage, so `ready_unprobed` outranks `ready_with_exceptions` — read `checkpoint_gates[]` for warnings rather than inferring them from status. Offline and CI runs need no flag: a transport error degrades to `ready_unprobed` rather than failing, because a 404 is evidence about the deployment while a transport error is evidence about the caller network. `--no-probe` is for hermetic runs that must make no outbound request. Second, `theme_gate.no_commerce_pages` no longer fires on a campaign whose declared funnel includes commerce pages that this build left out of scope, so a consumer that treated that code as proof of a content-only campaign was reading a build-scope artifact. Theme gate results gain `commerce_pages_out_of_scope`, and `scope_source` gains `doctor_derived_scope+spec_topologies`. Resolve remains a diagnostic command and still exits 0 on every status.

changes.summary: `qa resolve` gained --no-probe and --probe-timeout-ms, and two terminal statuses, routes_unresolved and ready_unprobed, alongside the existing ready / ready_with_exceptions / blocked. Probing the derived entry URLs is the default; --no-probe is for hermetic runs that must make no outbound request, since an offline run already degrades to ready_unprobed without it.

The Resolve section now documents route reachability: the full status ladder and why it is ordered by verification coverage, the five route_probe reason codes, the offline/CI degradation rule that separates an HTTP 404 from a transport error, the 25-URL probe cap, and the two route-root diagnoses emitted when every derived route is dead. It also records that resolve exits 0 on every status, routes_unresolved included.

The Theme Gate section now states that "ships commerce pages" is a property of the campaign rather than of one build: the gate reads built pages plus declared commerce pages this build left out of scope, the QA path unions the declared funnel into the doctor-derived scope, and commerce_pages_out_of_scope and the scope_source values are named.

entries.agent_impact: Browser QA now emits assertions for two things it previously said nothing about, and both can newly block a verdict that used to pass. A checkout page whose CampaignSpec declares exit_intent or promo_code_input with enabled: true gets browser-exit-intent-surface:<page> / browser-promo-code-surface:<page>: absent markup is FAIL/BLOCKER, markup carrying the declared offer_code is PASS, markup that cannot be tied to that code (or a coupon input behind an unopened disclosure) is MANUAL_REVIEW/WARN, and a browser collector that threw mid-read is SKIPPED with the cause rather than blocking. Typed-card runs additionally emit browser-order-display-parity:<plan> and browser-order-total-parity:<plan>, reconciling the persisted order pre-upsell read-back against what the checkout displayed at submit; a non-upsell line whose package was never rendered as selected, a displayed package that was never charged, or a total that disagrees with the displayed summary total is FAIL/BLOCKER naming the package ids. Both reconciliation assertions report SKIPPED with a stated reason when the page gives them nothing comparable - a summary whose rows do not all carry data-package-id, or a checkout with no [data-next-display="cart.total"] surface - and a consumer must read that as missing coverage, never as a pass. Both sets reuse the existing browser-runtime and browser-test-order families, so the verdict schema, QA_ASSERTION_FAMILY_VOCABULARY, and any allowlist keyed off it are unchanged. A campaign that declares a surface it did not build, or charges a package it never displayed, will now block where it previously reported ready.
entries.migration: none. A verdict that newly blocks is reporting a defect that was always there; fix the build or drop the undelivered declaration from CampaignSpec.

changes.summary: The QA skill records the four new assertion ids, their severity split, and the rule that a SKIPPED reconciliation is missing coverage rather than a pass; version 1.0.3 -> 1.1.0.
next-campaigns-qa is published at 1.1.0, so an installer can tell a build that asserts declared offer surfaces and order/display parity from one that does not.

entries.agent_impact: No runtime behavior changes. The repository guard that scans the shipped package for private strings (scripts/check-private-strings.mjs) now also forbids internal issue-tracker IDs matching SELL-<n> and NEXTON-<n>, so a future change that carries one into public-facing text fails the check instead of shipping. Enforcing it required scrubbing seven pre-existing leaks that were already published: an internal tracker-ID prefix on R2-Bx defect-slot comments in src/cli.mjs (six occurrences) and src/doctor-demo-ref.test.mjs (one). Those edits are code comments only; the R2-Bx slot labels are kept. No CLI command, subcommand, flag, output field, or exit code changes, and no consumer needs to re-pin anything.

changes.summary: Comment-only scrub: an internal tracker-ID prefix is removed from six R2-Bx defect-slot comments. No command, flag, output, or exit code is affected.

entries.agent_impact: The runtime recipe now states the guarantee its network policy actually makes. No declared field changed — install remains allowlist against registry.npmjs.org, build remains deny, the cache remains consumer-owned, and inherited proxy/credential/npmrc configuration is still refused — so an existing consumer's behaviour is unchanged and no action is required. The prose previously invited reading 'allowlist' as a host-level network sandbox; it is a package-manager configuration bound, and what prevents third-party code from disregarding it is --ignore-scripts on both steps, not the network layer. A consumer that added a real sandbox on the strength of the old wording remains correct and is now explicitly encouraged; a consumer that treated the hosts as advisory was already in violation and still is.

entries.agent_impact: Campaigns Agent and migration CI can now consume one strict, portable five-artifact sidecar bundle without depending on Campaigns OS internals. The root build packet selects the bundle by its generated_at value, canonical sidecars carry explicit schema identities and cross-artifact campaign identity, doctor evidence must be refreshed at the checked-out state, and historical QA may enter the bundle only through an explicitly selected full verdict. The new bundle check emits exact file hashes plus a material digest whose exclusions are contract-declared timestamps and run identifiers; markdown and filesystem mtimes are never substitutes for JSON evidence.

entries.agent_impact: The worst-case number of real orders a qa run places drops. RL-0022 recorded that a run may place up to twice as many real orders as --max-test-orders plans; it no longer can. A failed typed-card path is classified before it is re-run, and only a failure the runner can prove happened before submit is re-run. A failure after the order was created — a receipt whose line items are not buyer-visible is the common one — is inspected read-only against the order that already exists and never resubmitted, so a receipt-only failure no longer buys twice. An outcome the runner cannot prove either way stops the path and names an operator check instead of resubmitting. Two dispositions change for a consumer reading verdicts: a previously flaky post-creation failure that used to pass on a second real order now passes only if the read-only recovery pass clears it, and otherwise blocks; and a run can now stop a planned path with an explicit order-creation budget assertion, which is a safety stop the runner chose and must not be dispatched as a checkout repair. Read assertion evidence.order_creation for the classification and for two counts that are not interchangeable: submissions_reserved, the platform-side creation slots charged to the path, whether reserved before a submit click or charged for a hosted-checkout redirect where no submit click happens, which stand whether or not the create that followed succeeded, and orders_confirmed_created, the creates the platform was observed to accept. A spent slot with no confirmed order is the ambiguous case, not an order to reconcile. Read evidence.recovery to tell a recovered pass from a first-attempt pass. New flag qa run --max-order-creations <n>, defaulting to the planned path count and refused wherever a browser path builds its creation budget (qa run and qa parity alike) when it is non-numeric, fractional, negative or zero; --max-test-orders keeps its existing meaning.
entries.migration: none for callers. Supervisors and operators reading verdicts should treat a browser-test-order failure carrying evidence.order_creation_budget as a safety stop rather than a checkout defect, and should expect one order per planned path rather than up to two.

changes.summary: Adds qa run --max-order-creations <n>, a hard bound on real order creations reserved immediately before each submit click and defaulting to the planned path count, and documents it beside the planned-path cap in the qa help block and the Build Packet test-order policy notes. --max-test-orders keeps its planned-path meaning. The flag is parsed and range-checked at the qa run entry, so an unusable value errors naming the flag instead of falling back to the default budget. The runner behind it classifies a failed typed-card path as not_created, created or ambiguous, re-runs only a provable pre-submit failure, and inspects a confirmed-created failure read-only instead of resubmitting it.

Separates the planned-path cap from the actual-creation budget and documents the three creation classifications, the read-only recovery pass for a confirmed-created failure, and that an ambiguous creation outcome is never resubmitted. Also records that creation is decided from the whole event log rather than the truncated evidence copy, that a re-run may not spend a creation slot a still-unrun planned path needs, that recovery clears only on persisted evidence it re-read on that pass, and what the separate submissions_reserved and orders_confirmed_created counts each mean.

Replaces the unconditional-retry rule with the classified behaviour: only a provable pre-submit failure is re-run, a confirmed-created failure is recovered read-only, an ambiguous outcome stops and names the operator check, and the creation budget is a safety stop rather than a checkout defect. Version 1.3.0.

entries.agent_impact: polish capture no longer turns a single failed cross-origin beacon-class request (a stale analytics pixel in a merchant tag container, typically) into polish.hidden_eager_media.capture_incomplete. Failed requests are attributed by origin and role: cross_origin_request_failed (a cross-origin request in the explicit beacon allowlist: ping, fetch, xhr, other, preflight) is recorded on the resource ledger and surfaced as a warning while the capture stays complete; dependency_request_failed (the document, any first-party resource, or any cross-origin resource outside that allowlist) still fails the collection and blocks unwaivably. The request_failed problem code is retired; a consumer matching on it should match the two attributed codes instead. A failed request is no longer also counted as transfer_size_unavailable. Page-load evidence gains measurement.warnings[] (route, viewport, warning problem_codes[], bounded failed_origins[], failed_origin_count) and polish capture text output prints a Capture warnings (not blocking) block. An assembly report carrying an older capture that was blocked on request_failed re-validates as capture_shape_invalid and needs a fresh polish capture, which it needed anyway.

Origins are re-validated as bare http(s) origins before printing.

New named failure codes: cart_entry_unresolved, cart_entry_control_missing, cart_entry_no_navigation, cart_empty_before_submit. A consumer reading the ladder by index must not assume opened_checkout is steps[0]; one matching a 45 s order_submitted timeout on an empty-cart funnel will now see the named code instead.

entries.agent_impact: A qa run that spends its --max-order-creations budget changes disposition and exit code. The assertion for the path the budget stopped was status fail / severity blocker, indistinguishable from a checkout the runner watched fail, so every budgeted run whose budget ran out before the last planned path finalized blocked and exited 4. It is now status manual_review / severity warn, the same vocabulary a hosted-checkout redirect uses for a path a human must decide, and such a run finalizes ready_with_exceptions. A consumer that treated a browser-test-order blocker as a checkout defect worth dispatching a repair for will stop doing so for budget stops; one that gates on disposition blocked or exit code 4 will now see ready_with_exceptions for these runs and must read exceptions[], where the unexercised path is listed, rather than assuming an unblocked run proved every planned path. The assertion id, family, expected/actual text and evidence.order_creation_budget are unchanged, and a genuine order-creation failure is still a blocker that blocks.
entries.migration: none. If you gate on disposition or exit code, read exceptions[] (or assertion status manual_review in family browser-test-order) to see which planned paths were not exercised; do not read an unblocked verdict as proof that every planned path ran.

changes.summary: Records the status and severity a budget stop carries (manual_review / warn, never a blocker fail), and the disposition a run that spends its order-creation budget finalizes (ready_with_exceptions, with the unexercised path in exceptions[]), beside the existing --max-order-creations description.

entries.agent_impact: The run-record closeout command qa run prints as "Required next" carries --no-remit whenever the attempt does not end the run session - a BLOCKED verdict, or any disposition this version does not recognise - and says why. Such an attempt keeps the run session open, so an agent executing the printed command verbatim no longer spends the session run_id on the interim record; the session close (the later ready auto-end, or run end) is then the first and only POST for that id and lands remit_state ok instead of failed. A session-ending verdict is unchanged: it auto-ends the session in the same process, before the printed command can run, so the command mints its own run_id and remits, exactly as it does with no session. An agent that pattern-matches the closeout command string must accept an optional --no-remit between --qa-verdict and --json. Separately, an auto-end whose own remit does not close now says so on stderr and names the local record to keep; it does not print a re-send command, because run-record --run-id reassembles from current disk state rather than reloading the written record, and a session s QA attempt references are gone once the session is cleared - on a run repaired across several attempts that command replaces the stored record with a thinner one and sends that. The same caveat is now stated beside the run_record_remit_recovery action an agent may already be following. Re-sending a persisted record is not implemented. Remit itself is unchanged on the wire - the docs that called the endpoint an upsert now state that it keeps one record per run_id and refuses a repeat POST for a stored id with 409, so retrying a send that failed is safe and re-sending one that succeeded is not. Which dispositions end a session is one exported set, SESSION_ENDING_DISPOSITIONS, read by both the auto-end and the closeout it prints; membership is enumerated rather than excluded, so a disposition from a newer or foreign verdict keeps the session open on both sides instead of leaving them to disagree over who owns the run_id.
entries.migration: none. Read the closeout command from next_actions rather than reconstructing it, and treat --no-remit as expected whenever the attempt did not end the session. Do not treat run-record --run-id as a re-send of a stored record: for a multi-attempt run, prefer the local record file until reload-and-resend exists.

changes.summary: qa run receives the CLI ambient run session it already resolved, so the closeout command it prints is built against the same session whose run_id the close will remit under; whenever the attempt does not end that session - blocked, or a disposition this version does not recognise - the command is emitted with --no-remit, the auto-end reading the same exported set. Values interpolated into the auto-end stderr notice are flattened to one line first, so a path or run id carrying a newline or an ANSI escape cannot split or forge the operator s only remit-failure signal. An auto-end whose remit did not close now reports that and names the record to keep, rather than advertising a reassembling run-record --run-id as a recovery.

States that the remit endpoint keeps one record per run_id and refuses a repeat POST for a stored id with 409 rather than upserting; records that the closeout printed for an attempt which does not end the session carries --no-remit because the session close owns that ids one accepted send, that a terminal verdict auto-ends first and so remits normally, and that the run_record_remit_recovery command reassembles rather than reloads, so it thins a multi-attempt record.
